clue.text: Time off is sacred — I had a break

indicators.note: the short phrase interrupts the word for sacred, breaking it open

parts.note: holy means sacred
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone justifies taking a day off as a sacred right after a hectic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like part of the definition but signals insertion: IDA goes inside HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a period of leave from work, a stretch of time away from duties.

clue.text: Paperwork finished without tears

parts.note: the Japanese craft is paper work done by folding alone, with no tearing or cutting

explanation.surface: Office admin completed without any crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping; it means rips, which folding art avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft folds paper into shapes without cutting or tearing it.

clue.text: Help province up country

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: Assistance for a region is raised by the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AIDNI. Northern Ireland is commonly called 'the Province' in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Stuffy serials need rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of serials are put down again in a new order

explanation.surface: Dull, old-fashioned television serials need a fresh script.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room is stale and lacking fresh ventilation.

clue.text: One beats by a very short distance

definitions.meaning: one who whisks, beating eggs or cream
to win by a ... is to win by the narrowest margin

explanation.surface: A runner just edges out a rival at the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One beats' reads as a winner; it is a kitchen whisker beating eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisker is idiomatically a tiny margin, and literally a whisking tool or person.

clue.text: Assassins who spare women?

definitions.meaning: those who hit only men would leave women alone

explanation.surface: A question whether hired killers spare the women.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: hit men, not women.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract killers are called this, and literally the phrase means striking males only.

clue.text: Give voice with opera cast in Asian city

parts.note: to sing is to give voice

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters of opera are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer performs with an opera company in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like an opera's performers; it rearranges OPERA into APORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is a city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula.

clue.text: Demanding to take dope during leave

indicators.note: the information word falls during, inside, the word for leave

parts.note: to exit is to leave
gen is British slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: Someone insists on taking drugs while on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs; here it means information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or urgent, requiring much attention.

clue.text: After rant, head arranged to punish humiliatingly

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these three words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: After an outburst, the chief sets out a humiliating punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating someone in tar and feathers was a mob punishment meant to shame them publicly.

clue.text: Perhaps hawk's attempt to catch rook

indicators.note: the word for attempt closes round the chess abbreviation, catching it

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A hawk tries to snatch a rook in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the hawk as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk is one example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Gamely implying lawn is inferior?

parts.note: the old indoor court game's name suggests the grass-court version is not the genuine article

explanation.surface: A sporting snob sniffs at the grass-court game.
explanation.walkthrough: Real tennis is the original indoor racket game; calling it 'real' implies lawn tennis is a lesser copy. 'Gamely' means 'in terms of games', not 'pluckily'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the historic court game pointedly contrasts it with lawn tennis, hinting the latter is second-rate.

clue.text: Site around area in Kensington, for one

indicators.note: the word for site is placed around the abbreviation for area

parts.note: a place is a site

explanation.surface: A building site surrounds some plot in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington Palace is a royal residence in London; 'Kensington' looks like a district but is the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Palace is an example of a royal residence of this kind.

clue.text: Do only mediocre cricketers have these?

definitions.text: Do only mediocre cricketers have these?

parts.words: Do only mediocre cricketers have these?
parts.note: mediocre suggests being merely middling, yet every cricketer has batting and bowling figures of this kind

explanation.surface: A question about whether only middling players get statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket records a player's batting and bowling averages, so every cricketer has them, not just mediocre ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket statistics are kept as runs per innings and runs conceded per wicket, both mean figures.

clue.text: Odd cardinal has funny ideas for a game

parts.note: five is an odd cardinal number

indicators.note: funny suggests these letters are being treated strangely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the church has eccentric notions about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd cardinal' looks like a strange churchman; it is an odd number. 'funny' rearranges IDEAS into ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-a-side is a small-team form of football, a recognised sport.

clue.text: Hated former editor keeping old car

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the abbreviation for editor holds the word for an old car inside it

parts.note: a crate is slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A former editor hated driving his old banger.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or curse, so execrated means loathed.

clue.text: Stupid to put toddlers on this?

definitions.meaning: informal British for foolish or crazy
the small pot toddlers sit on during toilet training

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an idea about toddlers is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty means daft in British slang and also names a child's chamber pot.

clue.text: Fairies showing personalities? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for personalities is not included

parts.note: selves are personalities, one's inner characters

explanation.surface: Fairies reveal their true characters, but not straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small magical folk of the same supernatural family as fairies.

clue.text: In talk, entice to accept shocking treatment

indicators.note: the word for entice takes in the treatment abbreviation

parts.note: to lure is to entice
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a shock treatment

explanation.surface: In a talk, someone is coaxed into agreeing to electric shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' means electrical, not outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture is a formal spoken address to an audience.

clue.text: Character that directs one elsewhere

definitions.meaning: a statement of someone's character for an employer
a ... in a text points the reader to another source

explanation.surface: A sign or symbol that sends the reader off to another place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a printed symbol; it is a character reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A testimonial vouching for someone, and a citation pointing to another work, are both called by this word.

clue.text: Compel men to go through broken fence

indicators.note: the soldiers' abbreviation passes into the middle of the rearranged letters
broken signals the letters of fence are smashed into a new order

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Men are forced to push through a broken fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges FENCE into ENFCE, which OR goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce is to impose or make compulsory, to force obedience.

clue.text: Revolutionary spray dispenser

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary
a mist is a fine spray

explanation.surface: A rebel's aerosol canister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispenser' looks like a spray can; it is a pharmacist who dispenses medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses prescriptions, and in Britain is commonly called by this word.

clue.text: Lament hit on head, calling in doctor

indicators.note: the medical officer is called into the middle of the word for a blow to the head

parts.note: to bean someone is to hit them on the head
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone moans after being hit on the head, summoning medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan is to grieve over or complain about something.

clue.text: Most worrying tooth decay, in a way

indicators.note: the dental term sits inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
caries is the medical term for tooth decay

explanation.surface: Tooth decay is the most worrying kind, in a certain sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like a hedge; it is the insertion indicator plus ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, so it means most alarming or frightening.

clue.text: One should not eat more quickly

definitions.meaning: someone who fasts, going without food
the comparative of fast, meaning quicker

explanation.surface: Advice that a person shouldn't bolt their food.
explanation.definitionFit: A person abstaining from food during a fast, and the comparative of quick, share this spelling.

clue.text: Take a turn round a kingdom

indicators.note: the word for taking a turn goes round the letter a

parts.note: to spin is to turn round

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a drive around a monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a constitutional monarchy with a reigning king.

clue.text: He sells at a knock-down price

definitions.text: He sells at a knock-down price

parts.words: He sells at a knock-down price
parts.note: a knock-down price sounds like a bargain, but here the gavel knocks down each lot

explanation.surface: A trader who sells goods cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'knock-down price' suggests a discount; literally it is the price at which the gavel is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a sale at a saleroom bangs a hammer to close each lot at its final bid.

clue.text: A throw of the dice rejected in centre of revolution

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the score is read backwards

parts.note: six is a throw of the die

explanation.surface: A dice roll is disallowed in the middle of a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising; it means rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which a body rotates.

clue.text: Vegan at first madly ardent to be green

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Vegan is used
madly signals the letters of ardent are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A vegan's passionate commitment to environmental causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdant describes lush land covered in fresh growing plants.

clue.text: Trifling sum for strip

definitions.meaning: slang for a paltry amount of money

explanation.surface: Someone takes their clothes off for very little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' suggests undressing; it is a comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a tiny payment, and the title of the long-running Charlie Brown cartoon.
